title: EventFlow lease fencing and graceful degradation for console metrics pipeline
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Problem: The real-time console metrics pipeline can see short-lived duplicate consumers and partition flaps during deploys or autoscaling events. When a consumer restarts or two instances briefly claim the same shard, we observe duplicated increments in tenant metrics, checkpoint races that move offsets backward, and transient spikes in per-tenant token billing. Current leases are optimistic and rely on external consensus which is brittle during GC pauses and cloud flakiness.

Goal: Add a robust lease-fencing layer and a graceful-degradation strategy so that shard handoffs are deterministic, duplicates are bounded, and noisy tenant storms do not violate SLOs. The feature should be compatible with the existing Kafka-like stream and our checkpointing model, support multi-tenant fairness, and allow staged rollout with observability hooks.
acceptance_criteria:
1) No observed duplicate event application after a consumer failover in a staged upgrade test harness (injection of restart flaps).
2) Metrics for processed_per_tenant, duplicate_detection_rate, and checkpoint_lag are exposed and show improvement vs baseline in canary region.
3) Graceful-degradation mode caps per-tenant ingest rate under extreme load without dropping high-priority system events.
4) Rollout toggle exists in Console and can be turned on/off per-cluster.
5) Integration tests for lease fencing, soft-eviction, and bounded replays are added to CI.
implementation_notes:
Design summary: Implement a small lease manager co-located with the consumer group coordinator that issues cryptographically signed fence tokens (epoch token) per lease. When a consumer renews a lease it must present its latest token when committing checkpoints and writing derived aggregates. Any consumer that sees a token older than the current epoch should abort in-flight batches and attempt controlled handoff.

Key components:
- Lease manager: issues epoch tokens, stores last-seen epoch in durable store (etcd).
- Fence token propagation: include epoch and signer id in every write/commit header.
- Checkpoint validation: when applying a checkpoint, storage validates token epoch >= stored epoch; lower epochs rejected and logged.
- Soft eviction: when a new lease is granted, existing consumer enters 'drain' window where it finishes in-flight batches but stops accepting new batches for the shard. Drain window length configurable per-shard.
- Graceful degradation: per-tenant token-bucket rate limiter in upstream ingress that falls back to priority queuing (system > enterprise > standard).

Trade-offs considered:
- Signed tokens add small CPU/latency overhead; we use compact HMAC with short keys to reduce cost.
- Using etcd for lease durability is slightly more operational overhead vs purely in-stream metadata, but simplifies cross-region failover and makes audits easy.
- Drain windows must be tuned: long windows reduce duplicates but can delay failover; we pick conservative defaults and expose to ops.
testing_plan:
1) Unit tests for token generation/validation and checkpoint rejection.
2) Integration harness: simulate consumer flaps, verify no duplicate writes and checkpoint monotonicity.
3) Chaos test: introduce network partitions and GC pauses to ensure lease manager recovers and fence tokens prevent split-brain writes.
4) Load test: validate per-tenant rate caps and priority behavior under tenant storm.
5) Canary: enable feature in a single region for non-critical customers, monitor duplicate_detection_rate, per-tenant latency, and billing deltas.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Merge guarded behind feature flag and add observability metrics. Phase 1: Enable in canary region with synthetic flaps. Phase 2: Gradual region expansion with 10% host increment and verify SLA. Phase 3: Default-on for all clusters after 2 weeks of stable metrics. A rollback toggle exists that disables fencing and reverts to previous lease behavior.
observability_and_metrics: Expose these new metrics to Console and Datadog: lease_epoch_changes, fence_token_validation_failures, duplicates_detected, checkpoint_rejects, per_tenant_rate_limited, drain_window_expirations. Add dashboard tile comparing baseline duplicate rate to post-rollout. Integrate alerts: duplicates_detected > 1/min for 5m triggers pager with runbook.
migration_and_backward_compatibility: Consumers without the new fencing will continue to work but will not receive the duplicate protection. We will allow mixed-mode during rollout: new consumers will accept older tokens for a grace period but will start rejecting checkpoints that prove a conflicting epoch. Provide a migration script to sweep legacy checkpoints and mark epoch for each shard to current baseline.
